span.span: A speech deepfake detector reports how likely a recording is synthetic, but a forensic analyst also asks which system produced it, whether two recordings share a source, and on what evidence the conclusion rests. We present VeriSpoof, an audio language model that unifies five forensic tasks — deepfake detection, generator attribution (generator, acoustic model and vocoder), recording-condition analysis, synthesized-span localisation and source verification — with one set of weights, and supports each decision with grounded rationales whose every statement can be independently verified. Every answer is a sentence whose likelihood is read out as a score, so detection and source verification need no separate heads and can be thresholded at an operating point. Every explanation consists of statements with an independent check: observations are measured on the waveform the model hears, synthesized spans come from labels, and the source profile from generator metadata. Counterfactual examples teach the decision to follow the stated evidence. On the 14 test sets of Speech-DF-Arena, VeriSpoof-Plus reaches 2.14% pooled EER, third of 28 systems and first among open-weight ones, and VeriSpoof-Base, trained on the official training splits of eight corpora only, reaches 4.43%, less than half the EER of the next open-weight detector. With the same weights, VeriSpoof-Plus decides whether two recordings from generators unseen in training share a source at 6.2% EER. Controlled studies show that the audio representation decides what is detected, the LLM how well two recordings are compared, and that source supervision is necessary for neural-codec fakes. Rationales can be checked statement by statement, catch partial fakes that the one-step answer misses (99.6 against 78.4% on PartialEdit), and determine the decision under edits never seen in training (99.5%). Only 29.7 M of the 2.85 B parameters are trained, so training fits a single 24 GB GPU with gradient checkpointing. Both models, the inference code, a demo, and VeriSpoof-Bench, the evaluation suite of all these questions, are released.
